subject: A trailing BEGIN block steals the sub's tail position → preceding statement gets VOID context (op/context.t t8)
description:
DIAGNOSED s319 (probe s319/pr-ctx.pl).  Narrow and isolated by an A/B probe:

  sub context { $cx = qw[void scalar list][wantarray + defined wantarray] }

  $_ = sub { context(); BEGIN { } }->();   perl: scalar   PCL: void    <-- BUG
  $_ = sub { context();           }->();   perl: scalar   PCL: scalar  <-- correct

So PCL's tail/void classification is RIGHT in general and wrong only when a
compile-time-only block trails the real last statement.  perl removes BEGIN at
compile time, so `context()` remains the sub's tail expression and inherits the
caller's (scalar) context; PCL still counts the BEGIN as a statement, making
`context()` non-tail, hence void.

FIX SHAPE: when determining a block's tail statement, SKIP compile-time-only
blocks — BEGIN, and by the same argument END / CHECK / INIT / UNITCHECK (they
do not contribute a runtime value either).  Do it in the tail/void classifier,
not per-call-site; the family rule is "phase blocks are not runtime statements
for value/context purposes" (CLAUDE.md 11 — one place, keyed on the mechanism).

CAUTION: this lives in the same void/tail machinery as CLAUDE.md §8's known
VOID_CTX sub-body-wrap regression and task #161.  Check whether fixing §8 first
changes this — the three may share a classifier.  Verify with the full gate +
sweep, not just the probe: a tail-position rule affects every sub's return value.

SCOREBOARD: op/context.t 7/1 vs perl 8/0 — this row is the whole gap; the file
goes OK when it is fixed.  NOT registered as XDIFF: it is a fix target.
